# Bamburgh Northumberland

Explore Bamburgh

A pristine beach, drifting sand dunes, snug eateries tucked away on street corners, and a magnificent castle view everywhere you turn. These are just a few of Bamburgh’s draws, not to mention its coastal setting in the county's AONB.


## **A castle view around every corner**

As the royal capital of the ancient kingdom of Northumbria, spell-binding Bamburgh holds a [history](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/historical-sites/history-heritage) worth discovering. All the while, awe-inspiring [Bamburgh Castle](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/attractions/historic-sites/bamburgh-castle) will be your backdrop, and you can wander down the main street, past Bamburgh's [cafes](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/food-drink/cafes) and towards the [village’s](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/towns-villages) landmark red phone box for an especially staggering and [scenic view](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/scenic-spots).

Dominant and dramatic on its rocky plateau, Bamburgh Castle’s imposing presence along [Northumberland’s coast](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/beaches) makes for a magical [walk](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/inspire-me/blogs/best-short-walks-in-northumberland-national-walkin) along the beach. Head here from [Seahouses](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/towns-villages/seahouses) using the castle as your guidepost and admire its setting behind the wild dunes that sway in the breeze. Enter the grounds of this iconic, medieval fortification, with impressive corridors, towering turrets and formidable [fortresses](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/castles). As you explore one of the most iconic [castles](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/castles) in northern England, learn about the castle’s turbulent past, as well as discovering an array of [events](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/events) are constantly happening at the castle, such as Dragon Hunts, Ghost Tours and even Outdoor Cinema Screenings if you stick around after sunset. The Armstrong family, owners of [Bamburgh Castle](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/attractions/historic-sites/bamburgh-castle), are dog lovers and the grounds at Bamburgh Castle are [dog friendly](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips/whos-visiting/pet-friendly) so you can even bring your four legged friend.

The castle isn’t the only chunk of history that Bamburgh Village has to offer. The [RNLI Grace Darling](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/culture/museums/rnli-grace-darling-museum) is a [museum](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/culture/museums) dedicated to Grace Horsley Darling, who participated in the rescue of nine men from a tragic shipwreck. She became Victorian Britain’s greatest heroine, and the profound event had a huge impact on the RNLI as we know it today.

Another must see is Bamburgh Ossuary which is located in a crypt below St Aidan's church and is the final resting place of the bones of people from the 6th & 7th century. Discover more about their fascinating history with a guided tour of the crypt.

Standing on Bamburgh Castle beach, looking out at the North Sea you can enjoy views of [Holy Island](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/holy-island) and the [Farne Islands](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/farne-islands). If you are visiting the Holy Island of Lindisfarne make sure to check the [safe crossing times](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips/while-youre-here/holy-island-crossing-times) as the island is cut of twice a day by the tides.

If you’re looking for a cuppa between beach walks, a cluster of [cafes](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/food-drink/cafes) line Bamburgh’s stone-front streets. Plus, the [village](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/towns-villages) offers high-end [restaurants](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/food-drink/restaurants) serving exquisite [seafood](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/food-drink/seafood) for those wanting to be wined and dined.

For the golfers amongst us Bamburgh Castle Golf Club is often called one of the most scenic [golf courses](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/activities/golf) in Britain with views of [Lindisfarne](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/holy-island), the [Farne Islands](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/inspire-me/blogs/five-things-to-know-before-you-visit-the-inner-far), the [Cheviots](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/scenic-spots/northumberland-national-park/cheviot-hills) and Bamburgh Castle.

If visiting by car there is [parking](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips/while-youre-here/parking) on Links Road, then it's just a [short walk](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/activities/walking-hiking/short-walks) into the village. For those that prefer to sit back and let someone else do the driving as they [travel](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips), Arriva run [regular buses](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips/while-youre-here/getting-around) to Bamburgh, so you can enjoy a car [free day](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/inspire-me/blogs/free-things-to-do-in-northumberland).

## [Beaches and coastline](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/beaches)

Admire blazing sunrises, discover hidden bays, and relish superb seafood on our pristine coastline. Spot our castles standing guard along our dramatic shoreline, and explore more than 30 miles of barely-trodden beaches.

[Explore More](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/beaches)

[![Castles-HERO](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/media/e5onyoxx/castles-hero.jpg)](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/castles)

## [Castles](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/castles)

The only time you want your holiday to end in ruins is when you visit Northumberland. Home to more castles than any other county in England so why not explore magnificent fortresses, stay in a haunted castle with ghostly grounds, or explore a ruined medieval castle in the array of enchanting castles in Northumberland.

[Explore More](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/castles)

[![Islands-Holy-Island-HERO-Credit-@janehuntley_photography](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/media/n4qjgfcw/islands-holy-island-hero-credit-janehuntley_photography.jpg)](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/holy-island)

## [Holy Island](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/holy-island)

This mysterious tidal island off Northumberland's coast becomes completely inaccessible when the tide covers its causeway. Once it's safe to cross, expect charming cafés, an ancient priory, and a castle that teeters on the coastline.

[Explore More](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/holy-island)

[![Grace Darling Musuem](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/media/3rbpbpan/grace-darling-musuem.webp)](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/culture/museums/rnli-grace-darling-museum)

## [RNLI Grace Darling Museum](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/culture/museums/rnli-grace-darling-museum)

A museum dedicated to Grace Darling, the fearless young woman who became a reluctant celebrity in 1838..

[Explore More](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/culture/museums/rnli-grace-darling-museum)

[![kid-lilidorei](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/media/3l2e4v0n/kid-lilidorei.jpg)](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips/whos-visiting/family-fun)

## [Family-friendly activities](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips/whos-visiting/family-fun)

Northumberland has something for the whole family, whatever the time of year. From [family-friendly historical sites](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/historical-sites "Historical sites for families") and [dark skies in Northumberland](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/darkskies "Stargaze with the family") to the [Northumberland coast](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/beaches "Take the family to the beach") and gorgeous beaches - plan your family trip with our recommendations and local knowledge.

[Explore More](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/travel-tips/whos-visiting/family-fun)

## **Choose your Bamburgh accommodation**

Looking for [accommodation in Bamburgh](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/stay/accommodation-in-bamburgh)? Take a look at our guide to places to stay in Bamburgh for the perfect inspiration. Sleep beneath the stars at a [camping and caravan park](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/stay/caravan-camping) in the surrounding [countryside](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/scenic-spots/countryside), curl up in a [B&B](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/stay/bed-breakfast) with sea views or, if [self-catering](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/stay/self-catering) is your style, take a look at the village’s elegant, castle-view, [cosy cottages](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/inspire-me/blogs/cosy-cottages-in-northumberland). So whether it’s places to stay near [Bamburgh Castle](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/attractions/historic-sites/bamburgh-castle), somewhere a little more off the beaten track, or a [weekend break](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/inspire-me/blogs/plan-your-weekend-break) near Bamburgh Golf Club, there are so many places to stay in Bamburgh.

## **Bamburgh FAQs**

Is Bamburgh in Scotland or England?

Bamburgh is a village in Northumberland, England.

What towns are near Bamburgh?

Nearby towns and villages include [Holy Island](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/holy-island), [Berwick](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/towns-villages/berwick-upon-tweed), [Alnwick](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/towns-villages/alnwick), [Seahouses](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/towns-villages/seahouses), [Ford & Etal](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/towns-villages/ford-etal), and St Abbs. All of these can be reached within half an hour or less, most easily by car.

Can you walk on the beach from Seahouses to Bamburgh?

Yes, you can walk along the beach from Seahouses to Bamburgh. It is approximately 3 miles one way.

What is special about Bamburgh Beach?

It's vast, unspoilt shoreline is uncrowded and backed by fabulous sand dunes and the magnificent [Bamburgh Castle](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/attractions/historic-sites/bamburgh-castle). It also commands sea views across to Lindisfarne, Holy Island and [Farne Islands](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/destinations/islands/farne-islands).

Are dogs allowed on Bamburgh beach?

Yes, dogs are allowed on Bamburgh Beach.

Is Bamburgh Castle a National Trust property?

No, Bamburgh Castle is privately owned and operates as a visitor attraction.

Who lives at Bamburgh Castle?

The Castle is owned by the Armstrong family. The downstairs is open to the public. There are areas of the Castle which are residential and holiday apartments.

Are there toilets at Bamburgh Castle?

Yes, Bamburgh Castle has toilets once you are through the admission gate, available for visitors only.

How much does it cost to get into Bamburgh Castle?

Adult £15.50, Children £7.65 (5-16yrs) Family (2+3) £41. Disabled £11.40 with free access for carer. [Click here](https://www.visitnorthumberland.com/explore/things-to-do/attractions/historic-sites/bamburgh-castle) for further information.

How much is it to park at Bamburgh?

Bamburgh Castle has its own car park, charges are £4 per day. To park in the main village car park is £7 for the day.

Can you access Bamburgh Beach with a wheelchair?

Yes, [Beach Access North East](https://beachaccessnortheast.org/bamburgh/) loan specialised equipment for disabled & elderly people across the North East.

generation_excerpts: Standing on Bamburgh Castle beach, looking out at the North Sea you can enjoy views of Holy Island and the Farne Islands. If you are visiting the Holy Island of Lindisfarne make sure to check the safe crossing times as the island is cut of twice a day by the tides.

Dominant and dramatic on its rocky plateau, Bamburgh Castle’s imposing presence along Northumberland’s coast makes for a magical walk along the beach. Head here from Seahouses using the castle as your guidepost and admire its setting behind the wild dunes that sway in the breeze. Enter the grounds of this iconic, medieval fortification, with impressive corridors, towering turrets and formidable fortresses. As you explore one of the most iconic castles in northern England, learn about the castle’s turbulent past, as well as discovering an array of events are constantly happening at the castle, such as Dragon Hunts, Ghost Tours and even Outdoor Cinema Screenings if you stick around after sunset. The Armstrong family, owners of Bamburgh Castle, are dog lovers and the grounds at Bamburgh Castle are dog friendly so you can even bring your four legged friend.

If visiting by car there is parking on Links Road, then it's just a short walk into the village. For those that prefer to sit back and let someone else do the driving as they travel, Arriva run regular buses to Bamburgh, so you can enjoy a car free day.
